I've saved the new release process to project memory: run `make release`, which tags and publishes. It replaces the old memory that said to push a `vYYYY.MM.N` tag on main and let CI publish. I kept the old entry as history instead of deleting it.

The `Makefile` on `main` doesn't have a `release` target yet. It only has `test` and `test-fast`. If the target is on another branch or hasn't been merged, `make release` will fail here until it lands. I put this in the memory too, so it gets checked again when the `Makefile` changes.
